business_problem: Gaea wanted to avoid the high upfront cost, rigid capacity planning, weak disaster recovery, and slow content delivery that come with self-built gaming infrastructure while developing and operating large online titles.
solution_summary: Baidu AI Cloud worked with Gaea Interactive Entertainment during the development of the game 'The Legend of Sword and Fairy 3D' to replace self-built infrastructure with a cloud architecture tuned for different game workloads. Combat services ran on custom cloud hosts with 3.2 GHz CPU and up to 400,000 PPS single-instance capacity, while login, chat, and payment services used standard instances sized for their own traffic patterns. Elastic scaling and minute-based, on-demand billing let Gaea expand capacity during promotions or user spikes without committing to permanent overprovisioning. Baidu's global CDN accelerated the transfer of game resources and updates, and Baidu LSS embedded live-streaming capability directly into the mobile client so players and streamers in mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan could use the same delivery backbone. Together, the cloud-host, CDN, and streaming stack gave Gaea a flexible platform for game operations, media distribution, and disaster-responsive scaling.

solution_components.name: LSS Cloud Live Streaming
solution_components.role: Adds integrated live-streaming services to the mobile game client for audiences in multiple regions.

data_flow: Game clients interact with combat, login, chat, and payment services that are deployed on different cloud-host configurations according to workload needs. Resource packages and updates are distributed through the CDN, while live-stream video flows through Baidu LSS so gameplay and streaming share a coordinated cloud-delivery backbone.
business_outcome: Gaea lowered early infrastructure cost, improved server performance and content delivery, and gained elastic operational control for both gameplay and live-stream experiences.
metrics: Core combat servers use 3.2 GHz cloud hosts with up to 400,000 PPS per instance.
